root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Accepted
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3

overview: White offers a pawn with 2.e4 and 4.f3, and after 4...exf3 5.Nxf3 has open lines, a lead in development and the f-file for Bc4, Bf4, Qe2 and castling, aiming at h7, f7 and the kingside. Black can defend with ...e6, ...c6, ...Bg4 or ...g6, consolidate the pawn and head for a better endgame. Engines consider White's compensation insufficient, so the opening scores through traps and attack below master level.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nxf3, Bc4, Bf4 and castle, using the open lines and the f-file
Attack h7 and f7 with Qe2, Ng5 and Bd3 and sacrifice on h7 or f7
Push g4 and h4 to open the kingside when Black castles

black_ideas.idea: Hold the pawn with ...e6, ...c6 or ...Bg4 and return the extra pawn only for a safe position
Trade pieces and head for an endgame with an extra pawn
Develop ...Bg4 and ...e6 and castle short without weaknesses

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White d4 and an open f-file against Black pawns on e6 and c6 or a g6 fianchetto

character.notes: Tactical and open, with White's attack coming at once and Black walking a tightrope in the opening.

gambit.notes: Black keeps the extra pawn with accurate defence; it is the classic example of a gambit that can be held.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider the compensation insufficient and the line is almost absent at top level; it scores through traps and surprise.

structure.notes: Central pawns come off and the f-file opens early; open lines for the pieces.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly choose it, and it is played for surprise and the attack.

level.notes: Dubious so never Beginner, with many defences to learn; attacking ideas are easy though.

sublines_that_differ.name: Lemberger Countergambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 e5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black counters on move three; the position differs sharply from the accepted lines.

sublines_that_differ.name: Rook Pawn Defence
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 h5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black prevents g4 with an odd-looking but playable move.

character.reason: Open tactical play with an attack against the king from move five.

gambit.reason: White gives a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Engines and strong players consider the compensation insufficient.

structure.reason: Open lines and files for the pieces from the opening.

approach.reason: Seldom played by strong players, chosen for surprise.

level.reason: Never Beginner when Dubious; many defences must be known.

plans.reason: White compensates the pawn with development and an attack.
